title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol: revealed will does not make faith a motive of the eternal good pleasure
pass_a_gloss: Nor by this distinction of ours do we make the secret will collide with the revealed: For the revealed indeed says, I will not save Peter without faith (namely preceding, as a means ordained unto effecting his salvation): but the revealed does not say, I will not save Peter without faith preceding as a motive or condition for forming my eternal good pleasure concerning the salvation of the same. It is not therefore rightly deduced from the revealed will of God that the election of Peter unto salvation was made from his antecedent faith.
pass_b_english: Nor does our distinction set the secret will against the revealed. The revealed does say, I will not save Peter without faith — namely preceding faith as a means ordained to effect his salvation. It does not say, I will not save Peter without preceding faith as a motive or condition for forming my eternal good pleasure about his salvation. So from the revealed will one cannot rightly deduce that Peter's election unto salvation was made from his antecedent faith.
source_text: Neque hac distinctione nostra collidimus arcanam voluntatem revelatae: Revelata siquidem dicit, Nolo Petrum salvare absque fide (scilicet praecedente, ut medio ad salutem ejus efficiendam ordinato): at revelata non dicit, Nolo Petrum servare absque fide praecedente tanquam motivo vel conditione ad formandum meum de ejusdem salute aeternum beneplacitum. Non igitur ex revelata Dei voluntate recte deducitur electio Petri ad salutem facta ex fide ejusdem antecedanea.
